What to look for in motorcycle jackets

  • Laminated beats drop-liner. A bonded waterproof membrane keeps the outer from soaking through and chilling you in sustained rain.
  • CE Level 2 armour. Insist on shoulder and elbow protectors, and budget for a back protector if one is not included.
  • Layering system. A removable thermal liner turns one jacket into a three-season solution for British weather.
  • Connection zip. A jacket-to-trouser zip stops your kit separating in a slide — buy matching pieces where possible.

Frequently asked questions

How much should I spend on motorcycle jackets?

Our catalogue spans £109.99 to £1,240. Budget options under £150 cover the essentials, the £150–£400 mid-range hits the sweet spot for most UK tourers, and premium picks above £400 add refinement, lighter materials and longer-term durability.

Which brands are worth considering?

Popular, well-reviewed brands in this category include Klim, Ixon, Rev'it, John, RST, Held. All are stocked by SportsBikeShop with UK warranty support.

Textile or leather?

Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes and thermal liners. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport touring. Many riders own both.

faq.q: Textile or leather for UK riding?
faq.a: Textile is the practical all-weather choice for UK touring thanks to waterproof membranes, ventilation and removable thermal liners that handle changeable British weather. Leather offers the best abrasion resistance for spirited, dry-weather sport riding but is heavy when wet and less versatile. Many riders own both, using textile for commuting and touring and leather for track days and dry blasts.

faq.q: What is the difference between laminated and drop-liner jackets?
faq.a: A laminated jacket bonds the waterproof membrane to the outer shell, so the outer cannot soak through and chill you in sustained rain. Premium picks like the Klim Badlands Pro and Rev'it Vertical use Gore-Tex laminates. Drop-liner jackets place the membrane inside, which is cheaper but lets the outer wet out and hold water, making it colder and slower to dry.

faq.q: What armour should a jacket have?
faq.a: Look for CE-certified shoulder and elbow protectors, ideally Level 2, which absorbs more impact energy than Level 1. Many jackets include these, but the back protector is often just a foam placeholder or sold separately, so budget to add a CE Level 2 back insert. The RST and Rev'it jackets in our list come with quality CE armour fitted.

faq.q: Do I need a connection zip?
faq.a: A jacket-to-trouser connection zip clips your jacket to matching trousers so the two cannot separate and ride up in a slide, keeping your back and hips covered. It is well worth having, especially for touring. Where possible buy a jacket and trousers from the same brand and range so the zips are compatible.

faq.q: How do I choose the right size?
faq.a: A riding jacket should be snug enough to hold the armour in place over your shoulders, elbows and back, but still allow a thin base layer underneath. Check the sleeve length in a riding position with arms forward, and make sure the armour sits on the joint rather than sliding around. Use each brand's size chart, as fit varies between makers.
